This suit is filed by the plaintiff against the defendants for the relief of permanent injunction with respect to suit property bearing site No.52, Khata No.588 out of Sy.No.92/2 situated at Rachenahalli Village, K.R.Puram Hobli, which is more-specifically described in the plaint schedule.

2. The case of the plaintiff in brief is as under:-
The property bearing Sy.No.92/2 measuring 2. acres situated at Rachnahalli Village,
K.R.Puram Hobli was originally belonging to one Krishnappa K, who is the husband of the defendant No.1 and father of defendant No.2 and 4.
He had executed registered GPA dated 3 / 13 O.S.No.6785/2017_Judgment 28/08/2001 infavour of one R.Lokesh to sell the suit property.

So, said GPA holder has entered the agreement of sale with P & T Department Employees Co-Operative Housing Society Ltd., on 24/01/1991 and since said agreement was not materialized and hence, said society has decided to sell the sites carved out of Sy.No.92/2.

entities.text: P & T Department Employees Co-Operative Housing Society Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Defendant No.3 was the Secretary of said Society.

So, said Lokesh being the GPA holder of original owner and defendant No.3/Secretary of said Society being confirming party have executed the registered sale deed dated 21/11/2001 in favour of plaintiff and put her into the possession of the suit property and subsequently her name is mutated in the BBMP records.
Hence, she is in possession of the suit property and paying necessary tax to the BBMP.

It is further case of the plaintiff that now said Lokesh and defendant No.3 by colluding with legal heirs of said Krishnappa tried to trespass the suit property by taking advantage of the absence of the plaintiff at suit property and also demolished the compound wall by removing the electrical poles.
Hence, plaintiff has approached the jurisdictional Sampigehalli Police Station and they have registered Cr.No.181/2017 for the offences punishable u/sec.447, 427, 420 read with 34 of IPC.

Now,
defendants are trying to interfere the peaceful possession of the plaintiff over the suit property.
Hence, cause of action arose to the plaintiff to file this suit.
So, plaintiff has prayed to grant permanent injunction against the defendants not to interfere her peaceful possession over the suit property.
During pendency of the suit she died, her LRs are brought on record.

sentences.text: On issuance of summons, defendants have appeared through their counsel.
Among them defendant No.1 and 2 filed their written statement.
Defendant No.4 also filed her written statement.
Defendant No.3 though appeared through his advocate has not chosen to file WS and contest the case.
Defendants in their written statement denied the averments of plaint in para-wise including cause of action.

In their written statement they denied about execution of registered GPA in favour of Lokesh by Krishnappa and also denied that said GPA holder has executed agreement of sale in favour of Society and also execution of registered sale deed in favour of plaintiff by said Society and said 5 / 13 O.S.No.6785/2017_Judgment GPA holder/Lokesh.
They denied the possession of the plaintiff over the suit property.
They also contended that they have inherited the suit property from Krishnappa as legal heirs and they are in possession of the suit property.

They have also contended that defendant No.4 has filed a suit in O.S.No.2091/2008 seeking partition and separate possession, which was dismissed by competent civil Court and hence, she filed RFA No.2116/2011 and it is pending before Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
They also contended that defendant No.4 has filed another suit in O.S.No.25810/2013 against purchasers of sites over said Survey numbers and said suit is pending.
So, with these grounds, they prayed to dismiss the suit with costs.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed the following Issues:-
(1) Whether the plaintiffs prove that they are in lawful and peaceful possession enjoyment of Suit Schedule property as on the date of suit?
(2) Whether plaintiffs further prove the alleged interference by the defendants with their peaceful possession of the Suit Schedule property?
(3) Whether plaintiffs are entitled for the relief of permanent injunction as prayed?
6 / 13 O.S.No.6785/2017_Judgment (4) Whether defendant No.1 and 2 prove that they are inherited the property along with defendant No.4 from one Sri.K.Krishnappa and they have continued to be in joint possession of the property?
(5) Whether defendant No.1 and 2 prove that General Power of Attorney executed in favour of R.Lokesh is false and fabricated?
(6) Whether the suit is bad for want of notice under Section 125 of Karnataka Co- Operative Societies Act?
(7) Whether the suit is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties?
(8) What order or decree?

sentences.text: In order to prove the case, P1(b) has got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked Ex.P-1 to 10 and also got marked Ex.P.11 to 19.

In order to rebut the case of the plaintiff, SPA holder of defendant No.4 has got examined himself as DW1 and got marked Ex.D.1 to 19 and later said evidence was discarded, since he was absent and not ready to undergo cross-examination.
6. I have heard the learned counsel for plaintiff.
There was no representation by advocate for defendants, hence their argument was taken as nil.
Perused the pleadings of the parties, oral and documentary evidence.

My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 :- In the Negative, Issue No.2 :- In the Negative, Issue No.3 :- In the Negative, Issues No.4 to 7 :- Does not Survive for consideration, Issue No.8 :- As per final order for the following:
7. ISSUES NO.4 TO 7:-
This suit is for bare injunction and defendants have not claimed the counterclaim.
So deciding these issues does not arise.
Hence, I hold that these issues does not survive for consideration.
8. ISSUE NO.1:-
The burden is upon the plaintiff to prove her possession over the suit property and in order to discharge said burden Plaintiff No.1(b) has got examined herself as PW1 and relied upon Ex.P1 to 19.

Ex.P1 is the Sale deed executed by R.Lokesh being the GPA holder of defendant No.1 and 2 and this sale deed is also executed by defendant No.3/Suresh as a Secretary of P & T Department Employees Co-Operative Housing Society Ltd., and as a confirming party to the sale deed.

entities.text: P & T Department Employees Co-Operative Housing Society Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Ex.P2 is the Possession Certificate stated to have been issued by said P & T Society.
9. It is specific case of the plaintiff that R.Lokesh was the GPA holder of original owner but said GPA is not 8 / 13 O.S.No.6785/2017_Judgment at all produced by the plaintiff.

It is also case of the plaintiff that said GPA holder has executed an agreement of sale in favour of P & T Department Employees Co- Operative Housing Society Ltd., but said agreement of sale is also not at all produced by her.

entities.text: P & T Department Employees Co- Operative Housing Society Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Defendants have disputed said GPA.

So, the plaintiff has to produce the alleged registered GPA as well as alleged agreement of sale to show that GPA holder as well as Secretary of said Society had a right to sell the suit property in favour of the plaintiff but non production of said documents is fatal to the case of the plaintiff.
Hence, the plaintiff has not proved that her vendors had a right to sell the suit property.
10. Though suit is for bare injunction but it is with respect to open site based on sale deed and hence, suit for bare injunction itself is not maintainable.

On this point, I rely upon the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in AIR 2008 SC 2033, Anathula Sudhakar Vs. P.Buchi Reddy(Dead) by Lrs and Ors., wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that 'if there is a cloud over the title then suit for bare injunction is not maintainable'.
11.

entities.text: Anathula Sudhakar Vs. P.Buchi Reddy(Dead) by Lrs and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, there is no material on record that the possession of the suit property was delivered to P & T Department Employees Co-Operative Housing Society Ltd.,.

entities.text: P & T Department Employees Co-Operative Housing Society Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: So, whether said Society can issue Possession Certificate in favour of the plaintiff is the question to be decided in suit for declaration.

Since plaintiff has not produced alleged GPA as well as Agreement of Sale in favour of Gayathri Devi G S vs Girija on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197278437/
4 said Society, I hold that Ex.P.1/Sale Deed and Ex.P.2/Possession Certificate are not at all sufficient to prove her possession over suit property.

entities.text: Gayathri Devi G S vs Girija
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. Ex.P3 is the B-Property Extract standing in the name of plaintiff and it appears that on the basis of Ex.P.1/sale deed, her name is mutated in BBMP records but this extract is proof for payment of tax but it cannot be considered as a proof to hold the possession of the party over the suit property.
Ex.P4 to 10 are the tax paid receipts are also not sufficient to consider the possession of the plaintiff over the suit property.

Ex.P12 to 18 are the photographs of layout over Sy.No.92/2 but these photographs are not at all sufficient to hold that plaintiff is in possession over the particular site i.e.,
suit property.
13. The plaintiff has produced FIR as per Ex.P.19 along with complaint copy but said complaint copy is not marked by the plaintiff.
In the plaint there is a specific pleading that Crime No.181/2017 is registered against defendants for the offences punishable u/sec.447, 427, 420 read with section 34 of IPC.
In this complaint there is a specific allegation that her property has been trespassed by defendants by removing electric poles etc.,.

Apart from that there is a specific allegation as under:-
'Now, I am not in the position to identify my possession since all sites are demolished and flattened.'

So, this contention of the plaintiff is sufficient to hold that as on the date of suit she was not in possession of the suit property and as per aforesaid well settled position of law that the suit for bare injunction without declaration itself is not at all maintainable.

14. The appropriate remedy available to the plaintiff is to file a suit for declaration of ownership and for the relief of possession against original owners of suit property i.e.,defendants No.1, 2 and 4.

Moreover, the plaintiff has made defendant No.3 a party to the suit in his individual capacity instead of making the P&T Department Employees Co-Operative Housing Society Ltd., as a party, which is represented by its Secretary/defendant No.3.

entities.text: P&T Department Employees Co-Operative Housing Society Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: So, considering evidence on record, I hold that plaintiff has 11 / 13 O.S.No.6785/2017_Judgment not proved her possession over the suit property.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Negative.
15. ISSUE NO.2:- Since, the plaintiff has not proved her possession over the suit property, question of interference to her peaceful possession from defendants does not arise.
Hence, I answer this issue in Negative.
16. ISSUE NO.3:-
In this case, the evidence of DW1 is discarded but evidence of PW1 is not at all sufficient to grant the relief of permanent injunction in her favour.

So,
considering the evidence of plaintiff, I hold that plaintiff is not at all entitle for any relief in this suit.
Hence, I answer issue No.3 in the Negative.
17. ISSUE NO.8:-

In view of my findings to the above issues, I proceed to pass the following:
  The suit of the plaintiff is hereby Gayathri Devi G S vs Girija on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197278437/
5  dismissed with costs.
